html:
The Nooksack, who call themselves Nuxwsa'7aq, are a Coast Salish people of the Nooksack River valley in northwestern Washington state, east of Bellingham and close to the Canadian border. Their own language is now extinct, and many families also have ties to the Sumas and other Stó:lō people of the Fraser valley.

They fished salmon on the river, hunted elk and gathered berries and roots on the slopes of Mount Baker. In 1855 they were counted among the peoples of the Treaty of Point Elliott, but they did not move to a reservation and stayed on their river. The United States recognised the Nooksack Indian Tribe only in 1973. Neighbours: Semiahmoo and Skagit.
